title: Forest resilience of Armenia, enhancing adaptation and rural green growth via mitigation (FAO/GCF, GCP/ARM/008/GCF)
summary: FAO and Armenia's Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU) implement this eight-year Green Climate Fund project in the two marzes with the highest forest degradation, Lori and Syunik. It aims to raise forest cover by 2.5 percent, cut rural fuelwood demand by at least 30 percent, and give communities a larger role in forest and natural-resource governance. The project also sets up forest nurseries and supports the national forest monitoring and assessment system.
activities: Climate-adaptive afforestation, reforestation and sustainable forest management with Hayantar SNCO
Forest nurseries (Hrazdan and Sisian) with seed cold-storage facilities
Community-led forest concessions and natural-resource governance
Fuelwood efficiency: improved woodstove design and national energy-efficiency standards
Updating forestry and climate curricula at universities and vocational schools
Support to the National Forest Monitoring and Assessment (NFMA) system
results: 103 ha afforested, 10 demonstration plots set up, over 570,000 seedlings produced (FAO fact sheet, 22 Oct 2025)
Four national energy-efficiency standards adopted (target was one)
Collect Earth survey of Armenian land categories completed; 100% of Year-1 and 50% of Year-2 NFMA field data collected

title: EU Green Agriculture Initiative in Armenia (EU-GAIA)
summary: EU-GAIA aims at inclusive growth in the northern border marzes of Armenia (Shirak, Lori, Tavush) by boosting green agriculture and local added value. UNDP supports three value chains (herbs, legumes, sheep) while the Austrian Development Agency runs a grant scheme for green and organic agribusinesses (EUR 2.47 million call in 2020).
activities: Grant call for green and organic agribusinesses in Shirak, Lori and Tavush (fruit, berry and vegetable value chains; legumes, herbs and sheep breeding)
Demo sites: Sheep Genetic Centre (Azatan, Shirak), Herbs Seedling Centre and pedigree sheep farm with RFID weighing
Vegetable production, collection and packaging centre 'Lorva Hatik' in Stepanavan (Lori)
Training of farmers (sheep breeding, herb and legume cultivation, business planning with ICARE)
COVID-19 response package (EUR 456,500) with tractors, seedlings, inputs and post-harvest support
results: More than 350 beneficiaries trained and more than 400 French meat-breed sheep imported and distributed (UNDP report via FAO platform)
80 beneficiaries selected, 60 already equipped (FAO platform entry)
About 20 t of elite legume seed distributed, yielding more than 200 t of legume seed
'Lorva Hatik' centre: about 25 ha under cultivation with collaborating farmers in 2022

title: World Bank Irrigation Dam Safety Projects (Dam Safety Project and Second Irrigation Dam Safety Project)
summary: Two linked World Bank projects reduced the risk of failure at Armenia's most dangerous irrigation dams. The first rehabilitated the 20 highest-risk dams (after dam failures in 1974, 1979 and 1994) and the second financed safety works at a further group of dams, with dam surveillance, emergency plans and institutional reform.
activities: Rehabilitation works at 20 priority dams (e.g. Arpilich, Aygedzor, Halavar, Azat, Vardakar, Tavshut, Sovetashen, David-Bek, Sevaberd, Aparan, Karnut, Mantash, Sarnakhbjur, Hakhum, Tavush, Gegardalich, Gegharkunik-2, Kakavadzor-2, Upper Bazmaberd, Herher)
First project ended with 27 dams rehabilitated (the 20 planned plus seven more); the second project targeted 47 further dams and completed 44; Kaps dam rehabilitation was handed to MCC
Emergency preparedness plans, operation and maintenance plans and monitoring equipment per dam
Legal framework (Water Code, law on dam safety) and a dam-safety regulatory function
results: 44 dams rehabilitated under the second project (94 percent of target)
Risk-reduction target for the 20 original dams reached in 2004

title: World Bank Water and Irrigation Services Enhancement (WISE) Program - Phase 1
summary: First six-year phase of a ten-year World Bank multi-phase program to modernise irrigation schemes and improve rural water supply in selected areas of Armenia, with national water-sector reform. Phase 1 will modernise 2-3 irrigation schemes chosen from a short-list of five, pilot rural water supply in unserved settlements and assess the Vorotan-Arpa-Sevan conveyance tunnel.
activities: Component 1: national water and irrigation/WSS strategies, tariff review, restructuring of the Water Supply Agency, WUA support, a national Irrigation Water Accounting and Adaptation Center
Component 2: rural water supply and sanitation for unserved rural settlements (about 650,000 people in 579 settlements are outside the Veolia Djur lease)
Component 3: modernisation of irrigation systems (short-list: Lower Hrazdan canal, Arzni-Shamiram canal, Kotayk canal, Lori canal, Debetavan canal) incl. SCADA
Technical and institutional assessment of the Vorotan-Arpa-Sevan conveyance tunnel

title: World Bank Irrigation System Enhancement Project (ISEP) and Additional Financing
summary: The project cut pumping energy and water losses in targeted irrigation schemes by converting four pump-fed schemes to gravity supply and upgrading outlet canals in 13 other pump-fed schemes, and installed a SCADA water-measurement system. Additional Financing supported the tertiary network of the Baghramyan-Norakert scheme.
activities: Pump-to-gravity conversion in four schemes: Baghramyan-Norakert, Geghardalich, Kaghtsrashen and Meghri
Upgrading of 57.26 km of outlet canals in 13 pump-based schemes
Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system and water-measurement devices
Support group for Water User Associations; project management
results: Meghri gravity scheme fully operational since April 2016 (686 ha, 3.7 GWh saved)
Water-loss savings of 21.44 million m3/year in rehabilitated canals (target 23.58)
Geghardalich scheme left incomplete at closing (community dispute with Goght); Kaghtsrashen completed but failed pressure tests

title: UNDP Transition to low carbon irrigation technologies for increased productivity, food security and enhanced livelihoods in Lori and Shirak regions of Armenia
summary: UNDP project (Japan-funded) installing energy-efficient pumps and, per UNDP reports, solar photovoltaic plants at three irrigation pumping stations in Lori and Shirak to cut energy use and expand irrigated land. It supports Armenia's NDC on emissions from irrigated agriculture.
activities: Supply and installation of energy-efficient centrifugal pumps at Ayrum-Chochkan, Chochkan (two-stage) and Benyamin pumping stations (ITB 095/23, Sept 2023)
Passportization (inventory) of the irrigation pipe network under the three stations
Grid-connected photovoltaic plants at the stations (UNDP press releases, search coverage)
results: UNDP-reported (July 2024, not independently verified): energy cost down 90 percent at the Lori stations and irrigation water cost price down 41 percent; irrigated area at Lori stations up from 1,900 ha by 200 ha

title: KfW Support Programme for Protected Areas - Armenia (incl. Ecoregional Conservation Programme, Javakheti Plateau; Caucasus Nature Fund support)
summary: German financial cooperation (BMZ via KfW) supports protected-area management and the socio-economic development of neighbouring communities in Armenia, with a long-running ecoregional programme in the Javakheti Plateau (Lake Arpi) and the regional Caucasus Nature Fund covering part of the operating costs of key protected areas. The 2026 first disbursements from the Caucasus Nature Fund went to Zangezur, Khosrov Forest, Dilijan and Lake Arpi.
activities: Planning and functional management of selected protected areas (equipment, infrastructure, plans)
Socio-economic development of communities bordering protected areas
Support to protected-area system reform and financial sustainability, including the Caucasus Nature Fund
Establishment of protected areas in the Javakheti Plateau (Lake Arpi National Park)

title: World Bank Irrigation Rehabilitation Emergency Project (IREP, with Additional Financing)
summary: An emergency project that re-lined primary canals in the Talin and Armavir irrigation schemes to cut water losses and create rural jobs. An Additional Financing extended it to six schemes and to tertiary canals in 19 communities in four marzes.
activities: Rehabilitation of 83.81 km of primary canals: 59.01 km of the Talin scheme (Aragatsotn and Armavir) and 24.80 km of the Armavir scheme
Additional Financing: primary and secondary canals in six schemes (incl. Arzni-Shamiram, Kasakh, Lower Hrazdan, Shirak main canal, Nalband canal) and 50 km of tertiary canals
Institutional support to WUAs and water supply agencies; WUA Support Group maintained GIS irrigation maps for all WUAs
results: About 118,000 water users estimated to benefit
Water losses in rehabilitated primary canals reduced; Armavir main canal fully rehabilitated (24.8 km)

title: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Land Resources and High Value Ecosystems in Lake Sevan Basin for Multiple Benefits (UNDP/GEF 10854)
summary: UNDP, with EPIU and WWF Armenia, implements this GEF project to promote land degradation neutrality and secure biodiversity in the Lake Sevan basin. Demonstration sites are in six consolidated communities in Gegharkunik and Vayots Dzor, with restoration of about 2,200 ha of degraded forest land and stronger management of Sevan National Park.
activities: Promote land degradation neutrality in the Lake Sevan basin landscape
Secure critical habitats for biodiversity services (including Sevan National Park management)
Biodiversity-friendly economic development and incentives for local communities
Restore about 2,200 ha of degraded forest land in coordination with the State Forestry Committee
Knowledge management, monitoring and evaluation

title: Strengthening land based adaptation capacity in communities adjacent to protected areas in Armenia (Adaptation Fund, EPIU)
summary: Adaptation Fund project implemented by EPIU to reduce the climate vulnerability of communities next to Khosrov Forest State Reserve (Ararat marz) and Dilijan National Park (Tavush marz). It introduced community-based, climate-smart agricultural practices in degraded areas, strengthened value chains and technology access, and built awareness and monitoring capacity on climate-smart agriculture and land degradation neutrality.
activities: Community-based climate-smart agricultural practices in degraded areas and buffer zones (USD 1.73 m)
Value chains and technology transfer for vulnerable rural communities (USD 0.34 m)
Awareness, capacity building, monitoring and decision-making on climate-smart agriculture and LDN (USD 0.2 m)

title: Community Agricultural Resource Management and Competitiveness Project (CARMAC I and II)
summary: CARMAC I and II introduced community-managed pasture and livestock management in mountain communities and later supported high-value agri-food value chains. CARMAC II trains 109 communities in managing 207,000 ha of community pasture, about 19 percent of the country's pastureland.
activities: Community pasture and livestock management systems with pasture and fodder assessments
Stock watering points and infrastructure on pastures
Value chain development for livestock and high-value agri-food products
results: 109 communities, about 65,000 households (285,000 people), 207,000 ha of community pasture reached (World Bank feature, 2021)
World Bank reports improved standing stock, vegetative cover productivity and household income

title: Yerevan Water Supply Improvement Project (EU Neighbourhood Investment Facility, EBRD, EIB)
summary: Rehabilitation of the Yerevan water distribution network and household connections to cut water losses and improve 24-hour supply, financed by EBRD and EIB loans and an EU grant and implemented by the operator Yerevan Djur. The EU announced completion in May 2026.
activities: Rehabilitation and construction of over 200 km of water mains and replacement of supply pipes; zoning of the network
Modernisation of nearly 19,000 household connections; installation of household water meters
Refurbishment of pumping stations; EIB also notes expansion of sewerage in Yerevan and several surrounding villages
results: Round-the-clock water supply, improved service quality and reduced water losses (EU Delegation, May 2026)

title: Mastara Reservoir (Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development / EDB) - World Bank preparation grant
summary: World Bank-administered grant prepared the Mastara reservoir on the Selav-Mastara river in Armavir marz: feasibility study, environmental and social impact assessment and resettlement plan, for later construction by the EFSD/EDB. The reservoir would add storage for the Armavir irrigation canal system and replace pumping with gravity supply.
activities: Feasibility study and preliminary design (reservoir about 10.2 million m3, dam about 30 m, concept stage)
Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (2018) and preliminary Resettlement Action Plan (Feb 2019)
Training of the Water Sector Projects Implementation Unit

title: Developing the Protected Area System of Armenia (UNDP/GEF 3762)
summary: UNDP/GEF project to expand Armenia's nature reserves so that ecosystems are better represented in the protected-area system. In Syunik it supported the creation of Khustup State Sanctuary and the enlargement of Zangezur State Sanctuary, formalised by a government decision of 19 December 2013.
activities: Rationalise the protected-area system and expand nature reserves
Map and agree borders of Khustup and Zangezur sanctuaries with adjacent communities
Institutional management capacity for protected areas
results: Government resolution N 1465-N (19 Dec 2013) approved the borders of Khustup State Sanctuary (new) and Zangezur State Sanctuary (expanded)

title: World Bank Yerevan Water and Wastewater Project (YWWP)
summary: The project supported a public-private partnership lease for Yerevan's water and wastewater services, financing priority investments by the lessee (Yerevan Djur) and technical assistance. It aimed at safe, continuous water supply for Yerevan and less wastewater pollution.
activities: YWWP Fund: priority rehabilitation investments in Yerevan's water and wastewater system, implemented by the lessee Yerevan Djur
Technical assistance and project management
Rehabilitation of wastewater collection schemes discharging to the Hrazdan River (tributary of the Araks); upgrade of the sewerage system in a peripheral district of Yerevan

title: AUA Waste Management Armenia 2022-2026 (EPR and source separation)
summary: A Swedish-funded programme run by AUA to build waste sector capacity: an extended producer responsibility (EPR) system for special waste streams, a national source-separation model piloted in Sevan town and other municipalities, and capacity building.
activities: Component 1: introduce EPR system for special waste streams (support to the Ministry of Environment, CEPA requirements)
Component 2: develop a national source-separation model and introduce it in Sevan town and other pilot municipalities
Component 3: sector capacity building and scale-up

title: KfW GAF Agricultural Finance III and support to agricultural insurance scheme
summary: KfW financed on-lending to agricultural MSMEs through Armenian banks (GAF Agricultural Finance III) and a premium subsidy scheme for agricultural insurance against extreme weather, part of the G7 InsuResilience initiative. Both are national financial instruments without a defined territory.
activities: Loan to Armenian commercial banks for agricultural MSME financing (executing agency National Mortgage Company)
Subsidy of insurance premiums for poor and vulnerable farm households (climate risk insurance)

title: Preparation of an Action Plan to Restore Lake Sevan (World Bank IDF grant)
summary: A World Bank-funded grant helped Armenia prepare the Lake Sevan Action Program (1996-98) for the phased restoration of the lake's ecological balance. The plan led to a dedicated law on Lake Sevan and the Lake Sevan Commission.
activities: Preparation of the Lake Sevan Action Program for the Restoration of the Ecological Balance of the Lake
Proposal to consolidate laws on the lake and its basin into one law
results: The Law on Lake Sevan was passed by the National Assembly (2001 per Groong; 2002 per other reports)

title: Climate-Adaptive Food Security Enhancement Project (CAFSEP)
summary: ADB grant to improve food security and climate resilience of vulnerable smallholder farmers in Shirak and Tavush through climate-sensitive energy solutions, better access to logistics hubs and climate-smart adaptation planning capacity of the Ministry of Economy.
activities: Climate-sensitive energy solutions in Shirak and Tavush
Better access to logistics hubs in targeted provinces
Capacity of the Ministry of Economy for climate-smart adaptation planning

title: Partnerships for Rural Prosperity (PRP)
summary: PRP was a five-year USAID programme to raise rural employment through community competitiveness, economic governance, workforce development and small infrastructure upgrades. It selected communities with economic potential, including border villages.
activities: Study of 300 communities to select about 100 with economic potential, including border villages
Capacity building of local entrepreneurs and access to finance for women, youth and vulnerable groups

title: EBRD Armenia Water Reservoirs Phase I Project (five reservoirs)
summary: First phase of a nationwide EBRD-backed programme to build five water reservoirs for irrigation and climate resilience in agribusiness-dependent areas. The Armenian government's 2021-2026 programme foresees 15 new reservoirs.
activities: Construction of five reservoirs: Artik, Astghadzor, Kassakh, Lichk and Yelpin
Environmental and social assessment (ESIA, ESMP) and resettlement framework disclosed on ebrd.com

title: Catalyzing Financial Sustainability of Armenia's Protected Areas System (UNDP/GEF 3945)
summary: UNDP/GEF project to secure long-term financial sustainability of Armenia's protected-area system, linked to the Caucasus Nature Fund / Caucasus Protected Areas Trust Fund. The sources found describe a system-level financing effort rather than site-specific works.
activities: Financing and business planning for the protected-area system

title: Grant to UNICEF for Natural and Technological Risks in Armenia (USAID/OFDA)
summary: Small USAID/OFDA grant to UNICEF on natural and technological risks in Armenia. The IATI record gives no description or location, and no other source was found.
